analysis:
Integration pass over 15 units. All changes are CI tooling for the advisory threat-review scanner (.github/scripts tests, threat_review/{bedrock,budget_runner,budget_scan,context,depth_policy,diagnostics}.py, the threat-model-review workflow) plus developer docs. None touch the provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody, attestation (TB-009), fan helper (TB-010) or the T-041 prefix cache, so no canonical threat-model asset, boundary or threat is regressed, and threat_ids are empty.

Security-relevant tooling changes seen:
- Bedrock 'workload' call policy: plan_calls admits planned calls plus one repair slot, capped by a 500-call emergency ceiling. Invalid policy, ceiling or token settings are rejected. Exceeding the ceiling raises BudgetStopped (fail-closed), and unplanned calls are blocked because the limit starts at 0. The fixed policy and fallback restrictions are unchanged.
- Manual paid dispatch and pr_number/review_depth inputs are removed. THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA comes only from the pull_request event. Reruns (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT>1) start no paid work and are not cleared. The scanner still runs from the trusted default branch with PR code treated as data.
- Diagnostics add only scalar counters and policy names, with no content leakage.
- Incomplete final results now explicitly require human review, and tests assert clean() is false.
- Depth routing moved to depth_policy.py. Cross-file uncertainty no longer triggers a redundant local Opus rescan, and it is replaced by targeted deepening of the batches that cite retained findings. Critical paths get Sol only. Tests assert that uncertainty still yields manual_review_reasons and clean()==False. This reduces review redundancy but does not demonstrably weaken the clearance gate. The CI-tooling coverage trade-off is outside the provider threat model.

Coverage limits: integration replay covered 79 of 154 units. depth_policy.py, the workflow YAML, merge_policy.py and the budget_runner callers of plan_calls were not fully visible. Open items for any later review of the tooling itself: confirm integrate() findings are merged into self.findings so they drive depth, confirm BudgetStopped from plan_calls is handled in run(), and confirm that depth_policy preserves path-based escalation. No concrete finding is supported.
